items.title: Chink Martin Interview, 1966-10-19
items.q: The name 'Chaint' appears only in the [INTERVIEWER] turn as a form of address to the interviewee. The interviewee never mentions 'Chaint' as a third party, nor does the text describe any relationship between the interviewee and a person named 'Chaint'.

ctx.x: Very good. Very good. Very good. Very good.

Well, before we get too far up towards Chicago and later dates, I just wanted to ask you one question, Chaint, that I've wondered about because I've heard people make some statements. As I do a little arithmetic here now, I would say that this time that you're doing your serenading under the window and all this kind of stuff over on Ursuline Street, if it wasn't right around the turn of the century, it certainly wasn't very long after it, was it? Pretty close afterwards there, after 1900 came in. Oh, yeah. So, in…

No, that was really wrong. I never did want to come out with that discussion, because you have so many people that contradict you about that. But when they tell you that a colored man can play a better strict temper than a white man, don't let nobody kid you about that. That really is a bad face lie. It's just somebody that brought that up, you understand what I mean? And it's just a reputation, more of a reputation than anything else. Because I played with bands, I played with bands in 1900, late, up until this…
